mechanism_narrative: An increase in the federal funds rate by more than 0.25% within a month signals a tightening monetary policy, leading to increased borrowing costs and reduced corporate earnings, which in turn results in negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower in tightening periods compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp rise in unemployment rate by more than 0.5% within a month indicates a weakening labor market, which negatively impacts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods of rising unemployment compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real estate sales (HOUST) over three months signals a strengthening demand in the housing market, which positively impacts related industries and overall economic growth, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of increasing real estate sales compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A decline in industrial production (INDPRO) by more than 1% over two months signals a weakening supply side of the economy, leading to reduced corporate earnings and negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods of declining industrial production compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is below 1% and CPI (CPIAUCSL) increases by more than 0.5% in a month, it indicates inflationary pressure without corresponding monetary tightening, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate further fiscal stimulus.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS < 1% and CPIAUCSL increases > 0.5% in 1 month
regime_hint: low interest rate environment with inflationary pressure
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of low interest rates with rising inflation compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When nonfarm payrolls (PAYEMS) increase by more than 200,000 in a month and the unemployment rate (UNRATE) decreases by more than 0.3%, it signals a strengthening labor market, which positively impacts consumer spending and corporate earnings, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS increases > 200,000 and UNRATE decreases > 0.3% in 1 month
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of strong labor market improvements compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained increase in real GDP (GDPC1) over two quarters signals a strengthening economy, which positively impacts corporate earnings and investor sentiment, leading to positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly higher in periods of increasing real GDP compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the federal funds rate (FEDFUNDS) is above 3% and the real GDP (GDPC1) growth rate is negative, it indicates a restrictive monetary policy in a contracting economy, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days as investors anticipate reduced corporate earnings.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS > 3% and GDPC1 growth rate is negative
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not significantly lower in periods of high interest rates with negative GDP growth compared to baseline (t-test p > 0.05).
